title: NOW I KNOW THE LORD IS GREATER

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"He said, 'Praise be to the LORD, who rescued you from the hand of the Egyptians
and of Pharaoh, and who rescued the people from the hand of the Egyptians. Now I
know that the LORD is greater than all other gods, for he did this to those who
had treated Israel arrogantly.'" - Ex 18:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"Now I know."

Jethro was a priest of Midian, a man with a religious background and presumably
his own convictions. And on hearing what God had done, he makes a confession:
the LORD is greater than all other gods.

We should be careful about how much we claim for this moment. The text does not
give us a full account of Jethro's inner life or say he abandoned everything
else. But it plainly records a man moving from hearing to knowing, and then to
praise.

Notice what convinced him. Not an argument. Not a debate about which religion
was correct. A report of what God had actually done.

That is often how faith begins. Peter tells believers to be ready to give a
reason for their hope (1 Pet 3:15), and reasons matter. But what most often
opens a heart is not winning an argument. It is hearing a credible account of God
at work in a real life.

Moses did not try to convert Jethro. He told him what happened. Jethro drew the
conclusion himself.

There may be someone in your life you have been trying to persuade. Consider
simply telling them what God has done for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you trying to argue someone into faith rather than telling your story?
2. What has God done in your life that you could simply report?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to speak plainly about what You have done and to trust You with
what happens in the hearer's heart. Amen.
